subject: Starlite onboarding: COI, W-9, and PO routing
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@starlite-cloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Starlite onboarding: COI, W-9, and PO routing

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for partnering with Redwood. Procurement is kicking off vendor setup on our side; to complete onboarding and issue a PO we need the following items from Starlite Cloud: 

- Certificate of Insurance (COI) covering:
  • Commercial General Liability (CG 0001 or equivalent): $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate
  • Errors & Omissions (E&O) / Professional Liability: $1,000,000
  • Cyber Liability (including privacy & network security): $2,000,000 (please note if M&R applies)
- COI must name Redwood Inference as Certificate Holder: Redwood Inference, Attn: Procurement, 1200 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103.
- Additional Insured endorsement and Waiver of Subrogation on the CG for work performed on behalf of Redwood (if available).
- If Cyber policy has a retroactive date, please include it on the certificate or in the endorsement notes.
- Completed vendor onboarding form (I attached the form we use on our side; you can return your equivalent).
- Completed W-9 (for US entities) or W-8 if applicable.
- Billing / remit instructions and your preferred invoicing cadence (monthly/quarterly).

PO & timing notes: once we have the COI + W-9 + vendor form, procurement will generate PO RDW-2026-0457 and route it to your billing contact. If you can confirm whether Starlite needs the PO before starting work or will accept an invoice referencing the PO after start, that helps us align timelines.

Please send the documents to procurement@redwood.com and cc me so I can track. If you have any questions about the COI language or limits, call me or Laura (cc'd).

Appreciate it — looking forward to getting this wrapped up this week if possible.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Manager, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0192

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the clear checklist. We're happy to proceed. 

Quick status update:
- W-9 (starlite_w9.pdf) attached — our tax team completed it.
- Vendor intake form (starlite_vendor_form_filled.pdf) attached; I filled the contact and remit sections.
- We asked our broker to issue the requested COI; they expect to return a draft COI by end of day tomorrow.

A couple of clarifying Qs from our side:
1) For Additional Insured, do you require the CG endorsement ISO form (CG 20 10 or equivalent), or will a blanket policy note suffice?
2) Is the PO number mandatory before starting the kickoff call, or can we proceed with a signed SOW and invoice referencing the forthcoming PO?

I'll cc our billing (purchasing@starlite-cloud.com) on the COI email. If you can confirm the AI endorsement preference, we'll push for the specific language.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Partnerships
Starlite Cloud

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@starlite-cloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Starlite onboarding: COI, W-9, and PO routing

Elena —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Answers below: 

1) Additional Insured: we prefer the standard ISO endorsement (CG 20 10 or equivalent) if the broker can provide it; that makes downstream verification faster. If not available, please include a policy endorsement explicitly naming Redwood Inference as Additional Insured for services performed under the SOW.

2) PO timing: procurement's preference is to issue PO RDW-2026-0457 before the first production milestone, but we can accept a signed SOW and initial work can begin if Starlite needs to mobilize earlier. In that case please include the PO number on subsequent invoices once issued. I'll confirm with Finance if there are any exceptions for advance billing.

One more ask: when the COI is issued, can the broker put the policy effective/expiration dates and any retroactive date (for claims-made cyber/E&O) on the certificate or attach endorsement language so we can confirm coverage continuity?

I'll hold on the kickoff call scheduling until we have the COI and W-9 in place — can you aim for sending the draft COI tomorrow so we can review quickly? If you prefer, we can run the certificate through our vendor portal when it's ready (procurement@redwood.com).

Thanks — copying Laura/Ben for visibility.

-Dylan
